Inﬂammation
Inﬂammatory responses are cornerstones in the pathophysiology of PE. In normal gestations, the modulation of the immune
response, with a hormonal/placental-induced shift from a T-helper (Th) 1 toward a Th2 immune response is needed for appropriate
development of pregnancy (Hegde, 1991; Sykes et al., 2012). Under normal conditions, naïve T-cells differentiate into regulatory
T cells (Treg) (Ghaebi et al., 2017), creating the shift toward a Th2 biased state. However, depending on the cytokine milieu, this
physiologic response could turn into the production of pro-inﬂammatory Th17 cells (Saito et al., 2010) and Th1 cells (Chau et al.,
2016), leading to adverse pregnancy outcomes.
